It is the largest [[For-profit hospital|for-profit]] [[Private hospital|private]] [[hospital network]] in India, with a network of 71 owned and managed hospitals.{{cite news |title=A $2 Billion Health Empire Run by Four Sisters Makes a Comeback |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-11-20/a-2-billion-health-empire-run-by-four-sisters-makes-a-comeback |access-date=3 June 2023 |work=Bloomberg |date=20 November 2018 |language=en |archive-date=22 November 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181122230610/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-11-20/a-2-billion-health-empire-run-by-four-sisters-makes-a-comeback |url-status=live }}{{cite news |title=Apollo Hospitals Enterprise Limited — Investor Presentation December 2022 |url=https://www.apollohospitals.com/apollo_pdf/AHEL-Investor-Presentation-December-22-INR.pdf |access-date=3 June 2023 |work=Apollo Hospitals |archive-date=3 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230603194934/https://www.apollohospitals.com/apollo_pdf/AHEL-Investor-Presentation-December-22-INR.pdf |url-status=live }} Along with the eponymous hospital chain, the company also operates [[pharmacy|pharmacies]], [[primary care]] and [[diagnosis|diagnostic]] centres, [[telehealth]] clinics, and [[digital healthcare]] services among others through its subsidiaries.{{cite news |last1=Somvanshi |first1=Kiran Kabtta |title=Apollo Hospitals adds to Nifty defensiveness |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/apollo-hospitals-adds-to-nifty-defensiveness/articleshow/89881353.cms |access-date=26 March 2022 |work=The Economic Times |date=28 February 2022 |archive-date=26 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220326190036/https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/apollo-hospitals-adds-to-nifty-defensiveness/articleshow/89881353.cms |url-status=live }} The company was founded by [[Prathap C. Reddy]] in 1983 as the first corporate healthcare provider in India. Several of Apollo's hospitals have been among the first in India to receive [[international healthcare accreditation]] by the America-based [[Joint Commission International]] (JCI){{cite web|title=Accreditation for 3 Apollo Hospital branches|date=10 May 2006|url=http://www.hindu.com/2006/05/10/stories/2006051003181300.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060628205820/http://www.hindu.com/2006/05/10/stories/2006051003181300.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=28 June 2006|website=[[The Hindu]]|access-date=11 November 2006}}{{cite web|url=http://www.jointcommissioninternational.org/about-jci/jci-accredited-organizations/|title=Joint Commission International Organizations|website=JCI|access-date=21 June 2020|archive-date=14 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200814111753/https://www.jointcommissioninternational.org/about-jci/jci-accredited-organizations/|url-status=live}} as well as [[National Accreditation Board for Hospitals & Healthcare Providers|NABH]] accreditation.{{cite web|url=http://nabh.co/frmViewAccreditedHosp.aspx|title=Apollo Hospitals accreditation|website=NABH|access-date=8 June 2017|archive-date=2 July 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170702084420/http://nabh.co/frmViewAccreditedHosp.aspx|url-status=live}} == History == Apollo Hospitals was founded by [[Prathap C. Apollo Hospitals Enterprise Limited is an Indian multinational healthcare group headquartered in Chennai. It is the largest for-profit private hospital network in India, with a network of 71 owned and managed hospitals. Along with the eponymous hospital chain, the company also operates pharmacies, primary care and diagnostic centres, telehealth clinics, and digital healthcare services among others through its subsidiaries.
The company was founded by Prathap C. Reddy in 1983 as the first corporate healthcare provider in India. Several of Apollo's hospitals have been among the first in India to receive international healthcare accreditation by the America-based Joint Commission International (JCI) as well as NABH accreditation.
